newsitem.title: UK: C&W welcomes continued China investment in HK Telecom.
newsitem.headline: C&W welcomes continued China investment in HK Telecom.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc said on Friday it welcomed planned Chinese investment in its Hongkong Telecom subsidiary.
"We welcome the proposed investment by China Everbright in Hongkong Telecom," said Brian Smith, chairman of Cable & Wireless Group and Hongkong Telecom.
"This substantial investment of Chinese state capital demonstrates continued confidence in Hongkong Telecom and Hong Kong through the 1997 transition and beyond."
Speculation of a deal between Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and a China partner had already intensified in the colony on Friday after trading in Hongkong Telecom shares was halted for half a day.
Trading in shares of CITIC Pacific, which holds eight percent of Hongkong Telecom, was also suspended on Friday. Cable and Wireless owns 58.5 percent of Hongkong Telecom.
Hongkong Telecom shares later resumed trade, rising HK$0.90 to HK$15.90. CITIC Pacific shares resumed trade up 30 HK cents at HK43.80.

CITIC Pacific, the second largest shareholder in Hongkong Telecom, has reached agreement in principle to sell its 7.74 percent stake to China Everbright Holdings for about HK$11.4 billion ($1.47 billion) in cash.
C&W described China Everbright as a "significant enterprise under the leadership of the state council of the People's Republic of China".
CITIC Pacific also has close ties to the Chinese state but C&W welcomed the reaffirmation of the link ahead of the July 1 transition to Chinese rule in Hong Kong.
More than 150 years of British rule in the colony will end at midnight on June 30. ($ = 7.745 Hong Kong Dollars)
